lxc_971da9f0608ef248.text: Visitors often notice outdoor life, plain talk, and shared national days.

lxc_5e3ffc9db66c07a6.text: Those first pictures sit on older foundations: First Nations Country, convict and settler history, distance, immigration, and mateship.

lxc_31b1fa33550043e0.text: Australian culture begins with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, also called First Nations peoples.

lxc_4d31c6254856444b.text: Their cultures are among the oldest continuing cultures on Earth.

lxc_1d49f29b3ae379b3.text: People have lived on this land for tens of thousands of years, long before British ships arrived.

lxc_1b34ba55160671a5.text: In the First Nations sense, Country is a living relationship with land, water, and the wider living world.

lxc_8e1d03b68d4ad97e.text: It is not only a place on a map.

lxc_b372e978e7e26e21.text: Welcome to Country and Acknowledgement of Country ceremonies show that this idea still shapes public life in cities such as Sydney and Melbourne.

lxc_96604b4307f10a48.text: Torres Strait Islander peoples also keep strong sea and island links across the Torres Strait, north of Queensland.

lxc_fa637bd30c1c0a62.text: In 1788 the First Fleet arrived in Sydney, New South Wales.

lxc_800a7a4f04a5582b.text: Eleven British ships brought convicts, officers, and supplies, and British colonisation and settler society grew from that landing.

lxc_76f8465cc98c5e74.text: Convict transportation and later free settlement changed land, law, and daily life across the continent.

lxc_36965991560037c1.text: From that history came strong talk about fairness.

lxc_184246e027160848.text: The fair go means people should get a fair chance.

lxc_b80ff6da691d47e4.text: Next to it sits tall poppy syndrome: the habit of cutting down someone who seems too proud or above others.

lxc_28b2cd7229e0b1b2.text: Together, these ideas push talk toward equal treatment, first names, and less ceremony than many visitors expect.

lxc_cd3d4e070074a57e.text: Australia is a huge country, and towns can sit far apart.

lxc_70591360222e1121.text: The bush means land away from easy city comfort — dry country, long roads, and small communities.

lxc_1fb67a2229aa91d6.text: Distance shaped practical habits: people plan travel carefully, look after neighbours, and talk often about weather, roads, and outdoor work.

lxc_00c998679937675f.text: On the coast, city life looks different but still outdoor.

lxc_215c0056835e8bc9.text: In Sydney and Melbourne, beach time, parks, barbecues, and weekend sport fill ordinary conversation.

lxc_a93fb77329eb1c44.text: Cricket, Australian rules football, and rugby league are common shared topics.

lxc_789f20c47c9f37a7.text: Distance and outdoor life both push people outside the house and into shared public space.

lxc_b941e6f1ff43724e.text: After World War II, large immigration waves changed Australian cities.

lxc_eac52e43eebff418.text: The White Australia policy, which had limited non-European migration, was dismantled across the 1960s and 1970s.

lxc_05c163c76d9b0458.text: From the 1970s onward, official multicultural policy grew, and new arrivals came from Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and the Pacific in large numbers.

lxc_eb7ccd16fb834145.text: Sydney and Melbourne became clear multicultural centres.

lxc_ee75855e44f1c943.text: In daily city life, visitors hear many languages and see restaurants, shops, and festivals from many family stories.

lxc_f471f64dff08072b.text: Food streets, suburban temples and churches, and weekend markets show how immigration remade ordinary Australian city culture.

lxc_23190d79b7c9b5da.text: Mateship is a famous Australian idea of loyal friendship and support between equals.

lxc_c6660ebbe280a6cd.text: It grew in bush work, wartime service, and everyday help between friends.

lxc_2754ec63349b68d8.text: The friendly word mate still appears in shops, workplaces, and street talk.

lxc_af67ecd883465b12.text: Because mateship values equals, manners often feel informal to visitors.

lxc_d095ae6e8e4becef.text: People may use first names quickly and get to the point in ordinary talk.

lxc_00919782a83731db.text: Direct talk usually means saying the main idea without long ceremony.

lxc_a5621ba0ff0e3c8f.text: Visitors who expect more formal openings can find Australian talk sudden at first, then clear and warm once the friendship pattern shows.

lxc_eb6fd8ea9eb7037f.text: It remembers the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps, or ANZAC, who landed at Gallipoli in 1915, and later service by Australian forces.

lxc_5b593739f449b1e7.text: Dawn services at war memorials, marches in towns and cities, and quiet morning gatherings give the day a shared national shape.

lxc_be9e4912b3f23a4c.text: Visitors also notice brighter public signs: the Sydney Opera House, Bondi Beach, and big sport weekends.

lxc_c17dfd02771cfe00.text: Those famous pictures travel well in films and tourism.

lxc_f5792bd31926f1fc.text: Anzac Day memory gives a more serious shared story beside them, so people learning Australian culture meet both outdoor energy and national remembrance.
